title: Choose the C# project/assembly model and discovery seam
status: Approved by the maintainer on 2026-09-06; planning decision, not production implementation
approved_decisions: One active recorded evaluation context per index; all applicable target frameworks coexist within it.
Project identity follows the workspace-relative project path; a move is removal plus discovery.
Semantic facts are scoped by project and target framework; physical indexed-file identity is shared.
Assembly metadata is associated with the evaluation unit, not used as the project identity.
A separate language-neutral discovery interface has Cargo and MSBuild adapters producing a metadata snapshot.
ModuleResolver consumes precomputed context, remains database-free, and never launches MSBuild.
Publish one coherent index revision; bounded partial coverage contains successes and explicit failures, not mixed old/new facts.
Reevaluate metadata on every index/reindex invocation and measure impact; queries do not evaluate projects.
Preserve current Rust discovery and attribution behavior behind the Cargo adapter; do not introduce Rust target/feature modeling here.
Source-only syntax has explicit physical-file ownership without a fabricated project or target framework; it cannot establish confirmed project-scoped semantics or be accidentally double-counted.
The ownership/schema cutover requires explicit index --rebuild; no guessed migration or query-triggered rebuild.
.NET Framework projects, including classic non-SDK projects, must work from day one. No SDK-only first release.

derived_model_constraints.logical_identity: Provider/language-discriminated workspace-relative project identity plus an adapter-normalized framework identity for an evaluation unit. Cache row IDs are not durable external identities.
derived_model_constraints.framework_identity: Framework identity cannot require the SDK TargetFramework property. Preserve evaluated identifier, version, profile and applicable platform qualifiers; classic .NET Framework projects may have empty TargetFramework and TargetFrameworks. Do not conflate profiles or OS-qualified frameworks.
derived_model_constraints.unavailable_identity: If framework enumeration or project evaluation fails, retain a project-level failure with explicit incomplete enumeration rather than fabricate an evaluation unit or call the empty set complete.
snapshot_contents: Recorded evaluation context and exact toolchain/restore provenance
Discovered project identities and enumeration completeness
Evaluation-unit identities and typed success/failure evidence
Effective source membership and physical versus logical Link paths
Evaluated parse-relevant properties including conditional symbols
Evaluated project/reference declarations and their metadata
derived_model_constraints.reference_evidence: A declared ProjectReference is not proof of a selected target-framework binding, resolved assembly path, or transitive semantic dependency. Preserve metadata and unresolved target selection explicitly; do not guess from assembly name, namespace, or matching TFM text.
derived_model_constraints.source_containment: Only physical inputs inside the canonical workspace are indexed. Link is not physical identity. Outside-workspace inputs make the affected evidence Indeterminate under the approved rvr5 contract.
derived_model_constraints.reevaluation: Changed metadata, membership or parse context invalidates affected unit facts and dependent analysis even when source bytes are unchanged. This does not claim a complete metadata-staleness detector or authorize static fallback to Confirmed.
derived_model_constraints.authority: Retain rvr5 evaluation-only, explicit trust, separate restore permission, exact compatible-host selection, and typed failure rules. LSP is non-authoritative. No design-time/build targets are silently introduced.

required_success_evidence: Classic non-SDK .NET Framework projects on compatible Windows MSBuild
Legacy framework version/profile without SDK TargetFramework
Explicit, imported and linked Compile items
Restored packages.config and PackageReference project shapes as applicable
Mixed SDK/classic solutions and solution configuration provenance
Project changes with unchanged C# source
Real legacy-host timing and resource measurements
day_one_framework_gate.release_rule: Indeterminate for every legacy input is not support. Successful real legacy cases and the approved semantic oracles are mandatory before first release; failure-only fixtures cannot substitute.
day_one_framework_gate.host_transport: Do not make dotnet msbuild or the MSBuild 17.8+ getProperty/getItem switches the discovery interface contract. The adapter must use an evaluation-only mechanism supported by the compatible host without relaxing trust or toolchain provenance.
day_one_framework_gate.local_proof_limit: This session has only the dotnet SDK host. Generated non-SDK evaluation on Linux does not qualify Windows MSBuild, Mono, packages.config restore, framework reference resolution, WPF/WinForms generated inputs, or real-repository semantic parity.
